From 5d4e8ae6e57b025802aadf55a4775c55cceb75f1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2024 11:45:21 +1000
Subject: [PATCH] nouveau/gsp: don't check devinit disable on GSP.

GSP should be handling this and I can see no evidence in opengpu
driver that this register should be touched.

Fixed acceleration on 2080 Ti GPUs.

Fixes: 15740541e8f0 ("drm/nouveau/devinit/tu102-: prepare for GSP-RM")

Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Danilo Krummrich <dakr@redhat.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240314014521.2695233-1-airlied@gmail.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/devinit/r535.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/devinit/r535.c
index 666eb93b1742..11b4c9c274a1 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/devinit/r535.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/devinit/r535.c
@@ -41,7 +41,6 @@ r535_devinit_new(const struct nvkm_devinit_func *hw,
 
 	rm->dtor = r535_devinit_dtor;
 	rm->post = hw->post;
-	rm->disable = hw->disable;
 
 	ret = nv50_devinit_new_(rm, device, type, inst, pdevinit);
 	if (ret)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/devinit/r535.c`**
   - The line `rm->disable = hw->disable;` has been removed. This change indicates that the `disable` function from the hardware structure (`hw`) is no longer being assigned to the `rm` structure in the `r535_devinit_new` function.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `r535.c` is aimed at ensuring that the GSP (Graphics Security Processor) handles the device initialization without checking the `devinit` disable state. By removing the assignment of the `disable` function, the patch suggests that the GSP is responsible for managing this aspect, which aligns with the goal of fixing acceleration issues specifically on 2080 Ti GPUs. This change is part of a broader effort to improve the functionality of the Nouveau driver, particularly in relation to the GSP-RM integration, as indicated by the fix reference in the patch description.

Here is the commit message:
nouveau/gsp: don't check devinit disable on GSP.

GSP should be handling this and I can see no evidence in opengpu
driver that this register should be touched.

Fixed acceleration on 2080 Ti GPUs.

Fixes: 15740541e8f0 ("drm/nouveau/devinit/tu102-: prepare for GSP-RM")

Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Danilo Krummrich <dakr@redhat.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240314014521.2695233-1-airlied@gmail.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the Nouveau driver incorrectly checking the `devinit` disable state, which should be managed by the GSP. This led to issues with GPU acceleration on 2080 Ti GPUs, as the driver was not properly coordinating with the GSP's handling of device initialization.

Here is the patch:
 
 int
 r535_devinit_new(const struct nvkm_devinit_func *hw,
 		 struct nvkm_device *device, enum nvkm_subdev_type type, int inst,
 		 struct nvkm_devinit **pdevinit)
 {
 	struct nvkm_devinit_func *rm;
 	int ret;
 
 	if (!(rm = kzalloc(sizeof(*rm), GFP_KERNEL)))
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	rm->dtor = r535_devinit_dtor;
 	rm->post = hw->post;
-	rm->disable = hw->disable;
 
 	ret = nv50_devinit_new_(rm, device, type, inst, pdevinit);
 	if (ret)
 		kfree(rm);
 
 	return ret;
 }
--

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
rm->disable = hw->disable;
```
Reason:
The Nouveau driver incorrectly assigns the `disable` function from `hw` to `rm`, which should not be managed by the driver but rather by the GSP. This mismanagement leads to improper coordination with the GSP's handling of device initialization, causing issues with GPU acceleration on 2080 Ti GPUs.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
// rm->disable = hw->disable; // This line is removed in the patch
```
Reason:
By removing the assignment of `hw->disable` to `rm->disable`, the driver no longer interferes with the GSP's management of the device initialization state. This allows the GSP to handle the `devinit` disable state correctly, fixing the acceleration issues on 2080 Ti GPUs.
